documents.title: Academic Affairs Principles for AI
documents.stance_why: The Academic Affairs page states that 'Faculty Expertise Guides Decisions About AI in Teaching' and 'Our goal is not to prescribe a single approach', so it sets no university rule and hands decisions to faculty. It offers no tiers or templates.
documents.summary: Academic Affairs principles say AI should support, not replace, learning; faculty decide course rules and must communicate them; students should gain AI literacy; and everyone stays accountable and transparent. It leaves concrete rules to instructors.

units.why: The framing sentence says the Guiding Principles are 'the foundation' and that these academic principles ensure AI 'strengthen' rather than 'compromise or diminish' education; it sets purpose and scope, so P56 and general phase.
units.anchor: the following principles guide our commitment to ensuring that AI serves to strengthen
units.frag_end: educational experience at the heart of our mission

units.why: The statement that education is about the learning process, 'asking questions, wrestling with complexity', explains why AI use is limited by the skill-building value of doing the work, so P41 and informs.
units.anchor: The process of learning — asking questions, wrestling with complexity, developing expertise

units.why: It says AI 'should be used' in ways that strengthen learning 'while preserving the intellectual work'; this ties AI use to protecting skill-building, so P41 rather than P32 because the stress is on preserving the work through which skills develop.
units.anchor: preserving the intellectual work through which students develop knowledge and skills
units.frag_start: AI should be used in ways

units.why: 'should complement, not replace, the human effort' tells people AI must not stand in for their effort; students remain the primary doer, so P32.
units.anchor: The use of AI should complement, not replace, the human effort required for meaningful learning.

units.why: 'Faculty members are best positioned to determine whether, when, and how AI tools support the learning objectives' hands the decision to faculty, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty members are best positioned to determine whether, when, and how AI tools

units.why: 'appropriate uses of AI will vary across courses, programs, and professions' gives the reason for not setting one rule; it supports per-course decisions, so P04 informs.
units.anchor: appropriate uses of AI will vary across courses, programs, and professions

units.why: 'affirms the role of faculty judgment in establishing expectations' is the university's statement that instructors set the AI rules, so P04.
units.anchor: affirms the role of faculty judgment in establishing expectations for AI use in their courses

units.why: 'Faculty should communicate clear guidance to students about when AI may be used' directs instructors to state their AI expectations; closest is P09 but it does not mention a syllabus.
units.anchor: Faculty should communicate clear guidance to students about when AI may be used
units.fit_note: Asks for clear guidance on when AI may be used, how, and when it is inconsistent with the course, but names no syllabus or assignment statement.

units.why: 'not to prescribe a single approach' states the university sets no uniform rule and encourages 'thoughtful engagement', so P04.
units.anchor: Our goal is not to prescribe a single approach to AI adoption

units.why: 'Preparing students for this future requires ... helping them to understand the capabilities, limitations, and implications' commits the university to AI literacy in the curriculum, so P70 rather than P44 because it is about teaching literacy, not use as a job skill.
units.anchor: Preparing students for this future requires more than teaching them how and when

units.why: 'Students should develop the ability to evaluate AI-generated information' asks students to critically evaluate output, matching P31 (verify AI output).
units.anchor: Students should develop the ability to evaluate AI-generated information, recognize potential biases
units.fit_note: Framed as a literacy goal students should develop, also covering ethical implications and judgment, not only checking output.

units.why: 'students should understand and evaluate the cost to our environment' names environmental harm of AI, so P53.
units.anchor: students should understand and evaluate the cost to our environment

units.why: 'The most successful graduates in an AI-enabled world will not simply know how to use technology' gives the career rationale for AI literacy, so P44 informs.
units.anchor: The most successful graduates in an AI-enabled world will not simply know
units.fit_note: Stresses evaluating and challenging AI and human judgment as the professional skill, more than using AI effectively.

units.why: 'AI tools do not replace responsibility for the work we produce' and 'accountable ... regardless of the extent of AI’s role' make students and faculty own what they submit, so P29.
units.anchor: faculty and students are accountable for the accuracy, quality, and integrity

units.why: 'thoughtful evaluation of AI-generated content' is listed as a minimum requirement of responsible use, so P31.
units.anchor: thoughtful evaluation of AI-generated content;

units.why: 'adherence to University academic integrity expectations' requires AI use to follow existing integrity rules, so P77 rather than P36 since no misconduct classification is stated.
units.anchor: adherence to University academic integrity expectations;
units.frag_start: adherence to University academic integrity expectations;
units.frag_end: adherence to University academic integrity expectations;

units.why: 'respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards' is a minimum condition of responsible academic AI use covering several concerns; P50 is nearest.
units.anchor: respect for intellectual property, privacy, and ethical standards.
units.fit_note: Combines intellectual property, privacy and ethical standards in one clause; type P50 covers only privacy and vetted tools.

units.why: 'The landscape of artificial intelligence will continue to evolve' with a commitment to support the community signals the position will change and support will be given, so P54.
units.anchor: The landscape of artificial intelligence will continue to evolve.
units.fit_note: Also commits to supporting faculty, students and staff in exploring AI, not only to revisiting the principles.

documents.unit: Initiative for Human Formation in an Age of AI
documents.title: Saint Joseph's University's Guiding Principles for AI
documents.stance_why: The page says 'They are not a policy' and describes values to 'guide judgment', not rules for particular uses, with disclosure only 'when expected by University policy (including course or syllabus requirements)'. The decision is left to other policies and instructors.
documents.summary: University-wide values (people-centered, privacy, fairness, environment, accountability, transparency) that guide AI use in coursework, teaching, research and operations. They say they are not a policy and defer to existing policies and course requirements.

units.why: The intro ties AI to the mission and says 'AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it', so students' own capacities stay primary: P32.
units.anchor: AI may support this development, but it cannot substitute for it.

units.why: 'clear understanding of how AI is reshaping the workplace and the professions our graduates will enter' gives the career rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: a clear understanding of how AI is reshaping the workplace and the professions
units.frag_start: we are committed to providing our community
units.fit_note: Commits the university to informing the community about AI in work, rather than saying courses teach AI use.

units.why: 'They are the values that should guide judgment whenever members of our community use AI tools, in coursework, teaching, research, or university operations' sets scope and purpose of a framework: P56.
units.anchor: They are the values that should guide judgment whenever members of our community use AI

units.why: 'They are not a policy, and do not replace the University's existing policies on data, privacy, or academic integrity' says existing rules continue to apply: P77.
units.anchor: They are not a policy, and do not replace the University's existing policies

units.why: Principle 1 says 'AI should augment human capability, not replace it', so people must remain the thinkers: P32.
units.anchor: AI should augment human capability, not replace it.

units.why: 'remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes' makes users keep the judging role over AI output: P31.
units.anchor: remain responsible for analyzing, questioning, and evaluating outcomes
units.frag_start: Members of our community should use AI

units.why: 'AI users must protect the privacy of others and sensitive or confidential University information' is a duty on personal and confidential data: P50.
units.anchor: AI users must protect the privacy of others and sensitive or confidential University information.
units.frag_start: AI users must protect the privacy

units.why: Those with data access must handle PII 'consistent with all applicable laws, regulations and University Policies', which is compliance with law and policy: P77.
units.anchor: ensure the use is consistent with all applicable laws, regulations and

units.why: 'should be mindful about what information they share with AI tools, understanding the distinction between data use in enterprise-approved AI tools and free or personal subscriptions' favors vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: understanding the distinction between data use in enterprise-approved AI tools and free or personal subscriptions
units.frag_start: members of our community should be mindful

units.why: 'Information entered into a public AI tool may not stay private' is a warning fact about prompts being stored or exposed: P50 informs.
units.anchor: Information entered into a public AI tool may not stay private.

units.why: 'AI outcomes should be evaluated for bias and unequal treatment' names bias as a concern users must check: P53.
units.anchor: AI outcomes should be evaluated for bias and unequal treatment
units.fit_note: Also extends bias to unequal access to the tool itself, which touches P51.

units.why: 'should consider who benefits and who might be disadvantaged by a given use of AI' asks for ethical consideration of harms: P53.
units.anchor: should consider who benefits and who might be disadvantaged by a given use of AI
units.frag_start: Members of our community should consider

units.why: Principle 4 says AI use 'carries a cost to the global environment' and that people 'should use AI deliberately rather than reflexively', an environmental-cost concern: P53.
units.anchor: should use AI deliberately rather than reflexively, weighing the resource cost of a given use
units.frag_start: Members of our community should use AI

units.why: 'Anyone who uses AI is responsible for the outcome' makes the user own the finished work or decision: P29.
units.anchor: Anyone who uses AI is responsible for the outcome

units.why: 'its output must be reviewed and verified, not taken on faith' because AI 'can be wrong, biased': P31.
units.anchor: its output must be reviewed and verified, not taken on faith

units.why: 'Use of AI should be disclosed when expected by University policy (including course or syllabus requirements)' makes disclosure follow other rules and not a blanket duty: P24 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Use of AI should be disclosed when expected by University policy
units.frag_start: Use of AI should be disclosed
units.fit_note: Disclosure is conditional on university, course, publisher, funder or legal requirements rather than required for every submission.

units.why: 'be able to explain how AI contributed to their work and how they exercised their own judgment' requires explaining contribution and judgment: P30.
units.anchor: be able to explain how AI contributed to their work and how they exercised
units.fit_note: Asks for explaining how AI contributed and how judgment was used, when disclosure is required, not every line of work.

notes: No school or computing policy found by collector. Both documents are principles, not rules for students directly.
